doc.title: Rudy Van Gelder — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Later career, remasters and other interests
title: Photography as a side passion and scanning old slides
summary: He took photographs while the house went up, returned to photography later, and likes digital scanning.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Looking back: no regrets, what it all meant

blocks.x: You also have a passion for photography.

Well, that’s a side issue. That’s what I used to do when I didn’t do this. It came in waves. Sometimes I was very interested, and totally ignored photography. In the early 60s I was taking pictures while this house was going up. But then later on, as things have slowed down, I switched my interest back to photography and I pursued that disciplined, with these pictures you see. So my connectivity…
It again has a digital aspect to it too, different than when you started photography, and it was getting out chemicals…
And now you like dealing in a digital age?

Oh, sure. It allows me to do things I couldn’t possibly do before, and don’t rely on. I don’t get too gadgety, or too artificial. I try to keep everything real. Occasionally I go back now to my own old slides. If I scan them and do them just right, they look beautiful. I have a nice collection that I can work on. Is there a similarity between audio, sort of?
It’s sort of re-mastering your slides.
That’s right, that’s what scanning is.
